prompt:
Write 11 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a hit while turning left claim, in time order. Injury: concussion. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1410; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- The patient was treated for the same body area within the last two years, and that condition adds to the current complaints.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The damage does not match the story: the dents are on another side and at another height than the described impact.
- The claimant later added small details, but the account stayed the same.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened after the insured reported a collision at an intersection where the vehicle was turning left and was struck by an oncoming car. The claimant has retained counsel, so all further contact will go through the attorney's office.

Entry 2: Police attended the scene and confirmed that the claimant was in the vehicle at the time. The other driver gave a statement that matches the reported sequence of events.

Entry 3: Scene photos and two independent witness statements were obtained and placed in the file. Both witnesses describe the impact as the claimant reported it.

Entry 4: The policy shows the driver of the vehicle is a named insured, and coverage was in force on the date of loss. Nothing in the underwriting history suggests a gap or lapse.

Entry 5: Inspection of the vehicle shows dents that sit on a different side and at a different height from the impact the claimant described. The pattern does not line up with the reported collision and needs further review.

Entry 6: Repair records and the prior claims database show no earlier damage to this vehicle. The question of whether the damage predates coverage has been checked and nothing points that way.

Entry 7: The claimant's medical records were requested through counsel. They show a concussion diagnosis, and the reported force of the crash is consistent with that kind of injury.

Entry 8: Records also show treatment for the same body area about eighteen months before this loss, and that earlier condition appears to add to the current complaints. A medical review has been requested.

Entry 9: Treatment followed a typical course, with frequency of visits reducing steadily as the claimant improved. The treating notes describe a gradual recovery.

Entry 10: Counsel sent a supplemental letter adding several small details about the moments before impact. The core account remained the same as the original statement, and the additions were noted in the file.

Entry 11: The file is being held open pending a reconciliation of the vehicle damage pattern with the reported impact, and the medical review. A coverage decision will follow once both items are complete.
